- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.00), model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect risk reversal or market panic.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +3–5% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen 3-day+ momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 10–15d average is > 72.0, cap forecast at 73.5; if < 70.0, floor at 70.5.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days triggers “lag correction”: delay 1–2 days in price rise forecasts to account for delayed market reaction.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often overshoots; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 10–20% of sentiment spike magnitude after 2 days.
